tool_input.title: Unify Toolbar Element Visual Consistency
tool_input.summary:
Fixed the remaining toolbar inconsistency caused by an invalid CSS selector for the settings zone.

Root cause:
- Selector used `#compose.sketchpad.toolbar.zone.settings`, but the actual ID contains dots.
- In CSS, dots in an ID selector are interpreted as class separators unless escaped.
- Result: settings-zone-specific normalization for toggle `data-state=on` never applied.

Fix:
- Replaced selector with exact ID attribute selector:
  - `[id="compose.sketchpad.toolbar.zone.settings"] [data-slot="toggle-group-item"][data-state="on"]`
  - same for `:hover`

Outcome:
- Settings controls (e.g., Filter Connectors/Models and Selection Additive/Subtractive) now share the same neutral style contract across groups.
- Tools-zone active group highlighting remains unchanged.

Validation:
- `npx tsc --noEmit --project compose/sketchpad/tsconfig.json` passed.
- `npm test --workspace elements/ui` passed (23/23).
- No linter errors in changed CSS file.

event.text:
You were absolutely right — this one was still not fixed.

I found the actual issue: my previous settings-zone selector was invalid for an ID that contains dots.

- Wrong: `#compose.sketchpad.toolbar.zone.settings`
- Correct: `[id="compose.sketchpad.toolbar.zone.settings"]`

Because of that, the normalization for settings toggles (`data-state="on"`) never applied, so `Filter` settings (`Connectors`, `Models`) still looked like a different style family.

### What I changed
In `elements/ui/globals.css`, I replaced both settings-zone rules with the exact-ID attribute selector:

- `[id="compose.sketchpad.toolbar.zone.settings"] [data-slot="toggle-group-item"][data-state="on"]`
- `[id="compose.sketchpad.toolbar.zone.settings"] [data-slot="toggle-group-item"][data-state="on"]:hover`

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit --project compose/sketchpad/tsconfig.json` ✅
- `npm test --workspace elements/ui` (23/23) ✅
- lints on changed file ✅

This keeps behavior unchanged and only targets visual style inside the toolbar settings zone.
